newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GE's Hungary bank unit sets 1996 dividend.
newsitem.headline: GE's Hungary bank unit sets 1996 dividend.

text.p: Hungary's Budapest Bank (BB), which is controlled by General Electric, on Wednesday set a dividend for 1996 of 120 forints per preference or ordinary share.

The decision, taken at the bank's annual general meeting, faces a challenge in the courts from some holders of preference shares who claim a legal right to dividend payments not paid since the shares were issued in 1992. Bank officials denied any breach of the law.

The preference shares, worth some 350 million forints at face value, were exchanged in 1992 for compensation coupons, which Hungary had issued to victims of injustice under the country's fascist and communist regimes.

The bank's registered capital amounts to 20.04 billion forints, of which General Electric Capital Services owns 27.4 percent. GE took a stake at the end of 1995 and controls Budapest Bank by agreement with the other shareholders. These include the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (32.4 percent) and the Hungarian government (22.8 percent).
Budapest Bank posted an after-tax profit of 5.22 billion forints in 1996 according to Hungarian Accounting Standards, up from 2.86 billion forints in 1995.
The shareholders' meeting decided to pay out 2.32 billion forints as dividend on 1996 and place 2.72 billion forints into the profit reserves. The balance goes into general reserves.

Chief Executive Officer Bela Singlovics told the meeting that the bank's balance sheet total rose six percent in nominal value to 225 billion forints in 1996, but in real value it lost 15 percent, mainly due to stricter control on loan risks and lower demand for credit in a cool economy in 1996.
He said in 1997 the bank would continue the development of its products and services, the modernisation of its computer network and a cost-cutting programme.
Chairman George R. Tappert added that GE intended to intensify its support to Budapest Bank so as to help it to further improve its profitability.
BB is among Hungary's six largest banks by assets.
